ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, there is a vertical wire on each of the left side and the right side, which can be regarded as the left and right busbars at the two terminals of the power supply. The bottom power supply is labeled E, and the internal resistance is ignored. The upper branch goes from the left busbar successively through R1 to the upper middle node A, and then through R2 to the right busbar. The middle vertical branch goes downward from node A successively through R4, capacitor C to the lower middle node B. The right side of node B is connected to the right busbar through R3, and the left side is connected to the left busbar through switch S; the switch in the figure is initially open. Then reason: The capacitor is equivalent to an open circuit both in the initial long-term steady state and in the final long-term steady state after the switch is closed. When the initial switch is open and the steady state has been reached, there is no current in R4 and R3, so the potential of the upper plate of the capacitor is equal to the potential of node A, and the potential of the lower plate is equal to the potential of the right busbar. Node A is determined by the voltage division of R1 and R2 across power supply E. After the switch is closed and the steady state is reached again, the capacitor is still open-circuited, and there is no steady current in R4, so the upper plate of the capacitor is still equal to the potential of node A; while the lower plate of the capacitor is directly connected to the left busbar through the closed switch. Since the ideal power supply keeps the voltage between the left and right busbars as E, the magnitude of the change in the voltage across the capacitor is E. The magnitude of the change in the charge on the upper plate of the capacitor is C E. The upper plate of the capacitor can exchange charge with the external circuit only through R4, so the amount of charge passing through R4 over a long time is equal to the magnitude of the change in the charge of that plate of the capacitor, namely CE.

method.method_draft: Use steady-state node voltages before and after the switch closes. From the image, identify the left rail L and right rail R as the two battery terminals, the top branch as L–R1–node A–R2–R, the vertical branch as node A–R4–capacitor C–node B, node B connected through R3 to R, and switch S connecting B to L when closed. From the text, use that the source emf is E with negligible internal resistance and all resistors are fixed. In the initial long-time open-switch state, the capacitor is an open circuit, so no current flows through R4 or R3; hence the capacitor upper plate is at node A and lower plate is at R. Compute node A by the R1-R2 divider across the source. In the final long-time closed-switch state, the capacitor is again an open circuit, so no current flows through R4; the lower plate is now tied to L by the closed switch while the upper plate is still at node A of the same R1-R2 divider. Subtract initial and final upper-plate charges: the divider terms cancel, leaving a magnitude of charge through R4 equal to C times the source-terminal voltage, CE.
